meta.description: NequIP l_max ablation in miniature: power-spectrum invariants of a first-layer E(3) convolution, ridge-fitted to an analytic Morse + three-body potential, with feature-count and radial-capacity controls.
meta.alpha_selection: inner 75/25 train/validation split, 21-point log grid, refit at winner

checks.name: power-spectrum features are O(3) invariant
ground-truth energies are rotation invariant
[sw] three-body term carries a substantial share of the variance
[sw] a purely radial model has an irreducible floor
checks.detail: 12.3% of Var(E) unreachable with 560 radial invariants (nRMSE floor 0.3501)

checks.name: [rep] three-body term carries a substantial share of the variance
[rep] a purely radial model has an irreducible floor
checks.detail: 20.2% of Var(E) unreachable with 560 radial invariants (nRMSE floor 0.4492)

checks.name: SW kernel (c - c_0)^2 has exactly zero content above l = 2
checks.detail: max |a_l| for l>=3 is 2.94e-14 vs a_2 = 0.4000

checks.name: SW: l=1 removes more angular power than l=2 (the paper's ordering, in power terms)
checks.detail: l=1 62.5% vs l=2 37.5% of non-constant power

checks.name: repulsion kernel keeps significant power above l = 2
[sw] RMSE falls monotonically over l_max = 0, 1, 2
[rep] RMSE falls monotonically over l_max = 0, 1, 2

[sw] l_max=3 buys nothing over l_max=2 (target has no l=3 content)
checks.detail: factor 0.935 (<1 means l_max=3 is worse, as expected from the extra estimation variance)

checks.name: matched control gives l_max=0 the most features of any model
[sw] at matched P the l_max ordering survives (0 > 1 > 2)

checks.detail: matched-P factor 29.6 vs unmatched 24.8 (106% of the log-gain retained)
